briefings.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon Talks AI Boom, Bond Selloff | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that relentless global government borrowing and AI capital expenditure will create long-term inflation and credit risks, while urging policymakers to prioritize growth-oriented structural reforms like deregulation over ad hoc taxes.

briefings.title: Top-Heavy Stock Rally Dares Bonds
briefings.tldr: Wall Street drove stocks—including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq—to all-time highs, led by AI-linked stocks like Nvidia (nearing a $6 billion market cap), despite headwinds from elevated energy costs, interest rates, and soaring global debt.

briefings.title: JPMorgan, Ford to Invest Billions in Michigan Manufacturing
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase, Ford Motor Company, and Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer launched "Michigan Lift," an industrial innovation program backed by a $1 billion purchasing commitment from Ford to onshore advanced manufacturing and supply chains.

briefings.title: JPMorgan's Dimon, Gov. Whitmer and Ford's Farley Talk the Michigan Lift | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase, Ford, and the State of Michigan have launched Michigan LIFT (Launchpad for Industrial Innovation and Transformation) to onshore advanced manufacturing supply chains, secure critical components, and boost domestic industrial independence.

briefings.title: Jamie Dimon on The Axios Show | Full Interview
briefings.tldr: Jamie Dimon warns that geopolitical risk is at its highest level since World War II, arguing that America’s future depends on restoring "grit," fixing failing domestic policies for lower-income citizens, and managing the dual-edged sword of AI.

briefings.title: CEO Speaker Series With Jamie Dimon
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns that while the U.S. economy remains temporarily resilient, unsustainable fiscal deficits and massive geopolitical "tectonic plates" pose severe long-term risks.

briefings.title: 'GET THIS MACHINE GOING': Jamie Dimon calls for a new American industrial buildout
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is calling for a massive $1.5 trillion domestic and allied industrial buildout over the next decade to secure supply chains, while warning that underlying inflation risks make him "cautiously pessimistic" about the long-term economy.

briefings.title: FULL Q AND A: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon Delivers Remarks At Reagan National Economic Forum
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns that shifting global geopolitical tectonic plates dwarf short-term economic concerns, urging the U.S. to secure critical supply chains through smart industrial policy while aggressively reforming domestic bureaucracy to restore economic mobility for lower-income Americans.

briefings.title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon speaks at Reagan National Economic Forum — 5/29/2026
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns that shifting global geopolitics and domestic bureaucratic inertia are the greatest threats to Western democracy, urging the U.S. to deploy "smart industrial policy" to secure critical supply chains, enact aggressive regulatory reforms to spark GDP growth, and take a decisive stance against foreign adversaries.

briefings.title: Live podcast with Jamie Dimon - CEO of JPMorgan Chase  | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Jamie Dimon emphasizes that long-term corporate success is built on a "relentless" culture of grit, small autonomous teams, and high-integrity leadership, while warning that geopolitical fragmentation and slipping credit standards currently pose the greatest risks to global stability.

briefings.tldr: Markets are nearing record highs as traders focus on resilient bank earnings and a potential de-escalation in the Middle East, with Iran considering a pause in maritime shipments to keep peace talks on the table.

briefings.title: Jamie Dimon cautions that Iran war “increases the odds of bad economic outcomes”
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns that escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly involving Iran, and unsustainable U.S. federal deficits increase the likelihood of "bad economic outcomes" like stagflation.

briefings.title: Jamie Dimon on Trump, the war in Iran, and Epstein | The Axios Show
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns that geopolitical risks are at their highest level since World War II, while domestic success is threatened by a "softening" of American grit and a corporate leadership class too "chicken shit" to engage in honest policy debate.
